reviews.review:
Rusty Foodies takes the old game of tetris and makes it free-form, and introduces a deceptively cute story with dark connotations and equally dark humor about it. 

[h2]Language Selection[/h2]
Right off the bat, you'll note the game starts in Korean language. You have to do the following to reach [b]English[/b] story and menus:
From the [b]Main Menu[/b] select the 2nd Option 
-From the menu at the top of the screen, select the final option with a Display screen with a symbol in the center
-Pick the 1st item here and click the arrows to get to [b]English[/b]

[b]Suggestion for Dev[/b]: Please have Language options listed side-by-side in the corner of the main menu to immediately allow for switching. Something like [KR] [CH] [EN]

[h2]So, what are we doing tonight?[/h2]

[b]Story:[/b]
While it's not Pinky and the Brain, Rusty Foodies has the Saturday Morning cartoon-feel behind what looks like a modified game of tetris.

A dark and gritty tale unfolds, allowing for a revenge arc, and then, darker humor precedes this sentiment. Every other match tells us of the world in newspaper headlines talking about the weather, the unprecedent amount of issues plaguing the day and more. 

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
Remove the limitations you know about Tetris and make it possible for you to stack in Vertically as well as Horizontally across the playing field, with free-form placement of every piece. Each piece corresponds to food such as cheese, meat, hamburgers, hotdogs, etc., and these pieces do not mingle. Not that they can't, but rather, your non-furry friends are picky eaters. 

Now, add environmental difficulties such as flooding, poison, human interference and other navigable obstacles to make the game stand out as a tough little contender. 

The loop itself is [b][i]delicious[/i][/b] and come with both standard story and infinite mode.

[b]Sounds/Music:[/b]
To say the sound and music is good is an understatement. There's truly notable level of production value, from sound effects, cheering cockroaches to the music that has the depth that only registers as orchestrated. 

It's a treat.

[b]Verdict:[/b]
It was pure chance that I found this game in the demos before release, but it stood out enough for me to grab it. Having said that, this is one of those purchases I don't regret. I would buy other games from this studio in a heartbeat if they came with this level of masterful delivery. [b]Worthy[/b] is an understatement.
